reading.title: The Voices Behind the Switchboard
reading.intro_zh: 这篇短文不复述 John Gilbert 的医院电话反转，而是真实回顾“电话总机（exchange）”时代：人工接线员如何用插线接通每一通电话，以及这一职业的兴衰。改编自权威媒体 History（History.com）的报道。

source.title: The Rise and Fall of Telephone Operators

passage: Long before callers could dial a number themselves, every telephone conversation depended on a human intermediary seated at a manual exchange. When the first commercial switchboard opened in New Haven, Connecticut, in 1878, it served only twenty-one subscribers, yet it established a model that would shape communication for decades. To connect two people, an operator listened to the caller, identified the destination, and physically inserted a patch cord into the matching socket, momentarily holding the entire conversation in her hands. Long-distance calls required the local exchange to patch the call through to more distant exchanges, each connected by a further series of cables.

The earliest operators were boys, but they proved so unruly and inattentive that companies soon replaced them with women, whose calm and courteous manner suited the demanding work. The profession expanded dramatically, from roughly 88,000 operators in 1910 to about 235,000 by 1930, though the conditions were severe: rigid dress codes, constant supervision, and a rule requiring women to resign once they married. During the First World War, more than two hundred American operators, nicknamed the "Hello Girls," served near the front, frequently acting as translators between Allied forces. This indispensable workforce ultimately vanished because of its own technological context: by the 1930s, technology that allowed subscribers to dial without an operator had become widespread, enabling phone companies to slash their workforces, and by 1940 the number of operators had fallen below 200,000.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How modern smartphones replaced landline telephones worldwide.
Why long-distance calls remain expensive in many countries today.
The rise and eventual disappearance of human telephone operators.
How telephone companies trained boys to behave more politely.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文围绕人工电话接线员的兴起、工作方式、规模扩张，以及最终因自动拨号而消失，主旨是接线员这一职业的兴衰。

questions.question: How many subscribers did the first commercial switchboard in New Haven serve?
options: Only twenty-one subscribers.
About eighty-eight thousand subscribers.
More than two hundred subscribers.
Roughly two hundred thousand subscribers.
questions.explanation_zh: 第一段明确说 1878 年纽黑文的第一个商用交换台只服务 twenty-one subscribers（21 个用户）。

questions.question: According to the passage, why did the operator workforce ultimately disappear?
options: Because women were no longer willing to accept the strict rules.
Because long-distance calls became too difficult to relay.
Because the First World War removed most of the operators.
Because automatic dialing let subscribers connect calls without an operator.
questions.explanation_zh: 第二段指出，到 1930 年代，让用户无需接线员即可自行拨号的技术已经普及，电话公司随之大幅裁员，接线员队伍因此最终消失。

questions.question: What can be inferred about why companies replaced boy operators with women?
options: Women were willing to work for no wages at all.
Women were considered better suited to the patient, courteous demands of the job.
Boys were needed for the more profitable long-distance exchanges.
Boys refused to learn how to use the patch cords.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中说男孩 unruly and inattentive（粗野、不专心），而女性 calm and courteous manner 适合这份要求耐心的工作，可推断公司认为女性更胜任。

questions.question: In the passage, the word "indispensable" most nearly means:
options: easily replaced.
poorly organized.
absolutely essential.
highly profitable.
questions.explanation_zh: indispensable 意为“不可或缺的、必不可少的”，文中形容这支接线员队伍极其重要，故选 absolutely essential。

writing.intro_zh: 今天把 Lesson 39 的五个电话询问句式提升到 B2+：用 asked...whether... 问一个结果是否成立，用 refused to... 写有原则的拒绝，用 When he was alone,... 写独处时刻引出的正式行动，用 was inquiring about... 说明来电的正式来意，再用 would be allowed to... 在间接问句里询问许可。

patterns.title: asked ... whether ...
patterns.source: He asked his doctor whether his operation had been successful.
patterns.focus_zh: whether 引出间接 yes/no question，适合礼貌地询问一个结果是否成功或完成。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句较复杂的句子：在一个正式或紧张的情境里，写某人询问权威方（注册处、评审、机构）自己的申请、评估或项目是否最终成功，并加入时间或心理背景。
patterns.sample: Before the results were posted online, the anxious candidate asked the registrar whether her long-awaited application had finally been successful.
patterns.tip_zh: asked 后面可以接人，再用 whether 引出真正的问题；注意 whether 后面用陈述语序。

patterns.title: refused to ...
patterns.source: The doctor refused to do so.
patterns.focus_zh: refused to 表示明确拒绝做某事，语气比 did not 更坚定。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句较复杂的句子：写一位专业人士（接线员、职员、医生）出于规则或职业操守，坚决拒绝向外人透露机密或私人信息，并点出拒绝的依据。
patterns.sample: Citing strict privacy regulations, the experienced operator firmly refused to disclose another subscriber's confidential number to the persistent caller.
patterns.tip_zh: refused to 后面接动词原形；如果是隐私场景，可以补出 why 或具体边界。

patterns.title: When he was alone, ...
patterns.source: When he was alone, he telephoned the hospital exchange.
patterns.focus_zh: When 引导时间从句，先交代某个时刻或条件，再写主动作。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句较复杂的句子：用 When he was alone 开头，写某人在独处的关键时刻才进行一项需要隐秘或专注的行动（核实、求证、正式询问），并交代目的。
patterns.sample: When he was alone in the quiet office at last, he carefully telephoned the regional exchange to verify the disputed account before anyone could overhear.
patterns.tip_zh: 逗号前是时间背景，逗号后是主动作；不要把主句动词漏掉。

patterns.title: was inquiring about ...
patterns.source: He said he was inquiring about a certain patient.
patterns.focus_zh: was inquiring about 是正式电话或办公场景里说明来意的表达，比 asking about 更正式。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句较复杂的句子：写来电者或来访者用正式语气说明自己正在询问与自己相关的状态、进度或资格，体现现代隐私场景下只问自己信息的分寸。
patterns.sample: Speaking in a measured, professional tone, the visitor explained that he was inquiring about the current status of his own pending membership request.
patterns.tip_zh: about 后面接要询问的对象；现代隐私场景里最好加 own，说明只问自己的信息。

patterns.title: would be allowed to ...
patterns.source: He asked when Mr. Gilbert would be allowed to go home.
patterns.focus_zh: would be allowed to 用在间接问题里，表示“将被允许做某事”。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句较复杂的句子：在间接问句里写某人询问自己确切在什么时候、在什么条件下才会被允许参加、进入或获得某项资格。
patterns.sample: The newly admitted student politely asked the coordinator when exactly she would be allowed to attend the orientation meeting reserved for first-year members.
patterns.tip_zh: when 后面用陈述语序：she would be allowed to，不要写成 would she be allowed to。
